chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abu Abdullah al-Razi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Uthman, from Ahmad ibn Nooh, from the man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

Al-Harith al-A'war said to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): 'O Commander of the Faithful, by God, I love you.' He said to him: 'O Harith, if you love me, do not argue with me, do not play tricks on me, do not compete with me, do not tease me, do not belittle me, do not act proudly with me.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali
key_terms.الْحَارِثُ الْأَعْوَرُ: Al-Harith al-A'war, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.تُرَافِعْنِي: Do not act proudly/haughtily with me

ai.seo_question: What are the six things one should not do to someone if they truly love them, according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) defines the practical boundaries of *mawaddah* (affection) by listing six specific behaviors—arguing, trickery, competition, teasing, belittling, and pride—that invalidate true love. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis that love for the Ahl al-Bayt is not merely an emotional sentiment but is manifested through respectful and dignified interaction, avoiding actions that diminish the beloved's status.
